activity.title: Today, we're announcing our $4.1 million seed raise for Copperlane (YC W26) . Six months ago, I couldn't have imagined Athan Zhang and I would come this far. I think startups are special in how they reward people that work hard. If you're willing to put twice as much in, you’re able to get more than twice out. Here's what founding Copperlane has taught me: 1. The world is your oyster. When I first moved to SF, I realized how that there was still so much I didn’t know. YC, in particular, showed me that it is possible and that billion dollar companies can be built by two people hacking away in their apartment. Your struggle is real, but you’re not completely insane for thinking it’s possible. 2. Take calculated risks. People generally overestimate the downside and underestimate the upside of starting a company when you’re young. While you shouldn't drop out for the sake of doing so, I believe it’s valid to take calculated risks if there’s a reasonable chance for greater outcomes. 3. The joy is in the journey. At some point or another, when everything goes wrong, you’ll be forced to think hard on why you want to be a founder. When people ask, I still can’t exactly put into words why I chose to do so. Part of it is the freedom, the other part is just the amazing process and personal journey it takes you on. Thanks to our early believers ( Y Combinator , TQ Ventures , Harshita Arora , and more), customers (you know who you are), and friends. Always so grateful for this privilege to build. Now back to work. ❤️ P.S. We are growing quickly and hiring. DM or email brianna@copperlane.ai if you want to join a winning team. https://lnkd.in/eMHY_A_C ...more ...more

First post... kinda nervous We just won the Best Digital Forensics Hack at Hoya Hacks 2026! Two long nights later, we built "Fries in the Bag", an audio steganography tool. Fries in the bag lets you encode any small image or text into an audio file, and have the image or text be completely inaudible to human ears. The tool works by translating the files into binary and encoding the 1s and 0s as super high pitched beeps. The tool can then decode the message by detecting the frequencies with Fourier transforms. Watch the demo and try it out here: https://lnkd.in/e5PtCteQ Huge thank you to my teammates Daniel Yi , Eric Zou , and Yafee Khan for working so well together. Special acknowledgements to Cipher Tech Solutions, Inc. for sponsoring the track and Hoya Hacks for hosting the event. To many more. ...more

I turned 21 in a strange, unfamiliar place last week (that place being New Jersey) Why? To attend HackPrinceton Fall 2025 Me and my teamates Yehor Ivanenko , Daniel Yi and Ruslan Akmyradov wanted to dive deeper into our exploration of LLM-powered 3D model generation, and HackPrinceton felt like the perfect place to push the idea further. We built Suzanne, a 3D modeling AI assistant that lets you create and edit models conversationally. Instead of relying on complicated CAD workflows and expensive software, you can describe or photograph what you want and watch it take shape in real time, then refine it naturally until it’s fully 3D-print-ready, all directly in the browser. Current 3D tooling has a sharp learning curve and is costly, and that reality often blocks creativity for those who are just learning, Suzanne is our accessible solution. Tech Breakdown: - MCP routing for switching between multiple LLM tasks: planning, editing, and code generation ( 5 different AI models used in total ) - OpenSCAD code generation to produce accurate, editable, parametric geometry - WebAssembly compilation for image processing and exporting STL models directly in the browser - Hunyuan image-to-model generation for shape extraction from photos/camera - WebXR visualization to preview models at real scale in AR/VR - ElevenLabs voice responses for conversational modeling feedback and audio-based editing - Three.js + React (Typescript) UI for real-time rendering, interaction, and editing tools It was quite a challenge to implement in such a short amount of time, but we pulled it off successfully, check it out: https://lnkd.in/evUSfJFK (Try out photo model creation) https://lnkd.in/eg8RkWGc Thank you to the HackPrinceton organizers, the great people I met from Dedalus Labs , Amazon , Vibe Kanban , Capital One , Anthropic , Y Combinator , and for the support from Ryan L. from Major League Hacking along with all of the other sponsors and supporters. And with that, my time attending hackathons as a university student is officially over (for now). I couldn’t have asked for a better one to be my last. From the organizers to the mentors from HackPrinceton made this weekend unforgettable. See you around hacker community! Here's to LakerHacks 2026! ...more ...more

Vibe-Coding has already peaked. That’s why my team and I built the first Vibe-CADing tool. (Disclaimer: We are not responsible for any doors falling off.) At HackPrinceton , Suzanne was born - an AR CAD tool for working with 3D models using either manual editing or a voice assistant (aka “Jarvis”) to tweak objects. Our main objective? Cut the time between iterations. Just put on your VR/AR goggles, import your model, and adjust it on the spot if it needs modifications. Whether you’re an enthusiast printing your first MVP on a 3D printer or an engineer pitching a project to upper management, Suzanne will help you achieve your goal faster. Thrilled to announce we won Best Design at PennApps XXVI!🏆 Our winning project tackled a big question: What if we could eliminate news bias and show people what's actually happening in the world? This is exactly the problem myself, Jatin Punjabi , and Ruslan Akmyradov tackled this challenge by building noogie - a news aggregation platform that clusters stories from multiple sources to eliminate bias. noogie automatically scrapes hundreds of articles daily from major news sources. It then uses AI to analyze and group similar stories together, identifying when multiple outlets are covering the same event. Finally, it generates neutral, comprehensive headlines for each story cluster, giving users an unbiased view of what's actually happening. Under the hood, we used sentence-transformers to convert articles into embeddings, then leveraged FAISS vector indexing for efficient similarity detection and clustering. The platform integrates OpenAI's GPT-4 API to generate those neutral headlines, while the frontend visualizes story clusters as interactive nodes using D3.js. Built with TypeScript/React on the frontend and Python Flask for the backend, all powered by Supabase for scalable data storage. Huge thanks to my incredible teammates who made this all possible, especially as this was my first hackathon! Massive gratitude to the PennApps organizers, Major League Hacking , and the University of Pennsylvania for hosting the oldest collegiate-run hackathon in the world and creating such an inspiring environment for innovation. Check out our project on Devpost and Github below: - https://lnkd.in/gAhEeBUk - https://lnkd.in/g7NmXP_n Photo Credit: Ryan Lay ...more ...more

Volunteerism seems like a waste of time up until you actually do it; then you realize it isnt about who you are today- it’s more about who you will become. You never can foresee it. My parents would sign me up to volunteer and help the poor. As a teenager, I dreaded it. BUT every time I did it, the needle moved. I gradually acquited the desire for service, not from the recognition, but from the impact in the communities I served. When I was 18, I went to Caracus, Venezula, and we built homes for the homeless; wired homes so they could have power; dug wells for fresh water. We stayed with a Franciscan Priest whose life was dedicated to serving and protecting the poor. I’ve always carried that same spirit toward helping others. Perhaps its why I love mortgage and housing; we provide a pathway to safety, security and where love can abound: and that is in a home that someone owns. Fast forward to 2026, I flew to San Francisco with my 18 year old daughter Emilie, where she will fly to Thailand with a group of girls, to volunteer her time to teach English to children. What a full circle moment. This will shape her: into what? Only the Lordknows. It will be formative at a minimum; life changing at a maximum. However this influence takes shape, it will impact her work and future family; so that perhaps one day, she will be doing the same with her 18 year old. Life has a way of coming full circle; and today, it did just that.

It’s vital to not confuse open weight models with open source models. New and impressive open weight models are being released and used every day across the industry, but I’ve yet to hear about any serious truly open source (open data, open training code, open inference) models. Distillation makes this all even harder to reason about.
